sentences.text: Abhishek Maheshwaram vs Ms. Sindu Pendota on 11 December,

2024 
Author: P.Sam Koshy
Bench: P.Sam Koshy
 The Honourable Sri Justice P.Sam Koshy
 And
 The Honourable Sri Justice Namavarapu
 Rajeshwar Rao
 I.A.No.1 Of 2024 In/And F.C.A.No.61 Of 2020
Common Judgment

: 
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.Sam Koshy) Heard Mr. A.Tulasi Raj Gokul, learned counsel for the appellant and Ms. Bathina Anusha, learned counsel representing Mr. Shyam S.Agrawal, learned counsel for the respondent.

2. The instant is an appeal which has been filed under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act, 1984 challenging the order dated 08.05.2020 passed in O.P.No.46 of 2016 wherein a petition filed by the appellant/husband under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was allowed and a decree of divorce was granted dissolving the marriage between the appellant and the respondent dated 14.08.2014.

While allowing the said petition, the learned Family Court had also ordered for refund of an amount of Rs.10 lakhs paid by way of dowry, Rs.15,02,000/- towards marriage expenses and return of gold chain and gold ring worth Rs.42,500/-, in addition permanent alimony of Rs.10 lakhs was also awarded.

3. Pending the appeal before the High Court, the appellant and the respondent seems to have, at the behest of the elders in the family of both sides, resolved their disputes and have arrived at a settlement which has been brought down in writing and the terms and conditions of settlement are reproduced hereunder:
i.

The respondent, in pursuance of settlement or compromise arrived between the parties, unconditionally and unequivocally undertake to give up her claim or relinquish her right to claim the reliefs granted by the Principal Judge, Family Court cum Addl. Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad in O.P. No. 46 of 2018, under her counter claim such as the reliefs of permanent alimony of Rs. 10,00,000/-; return of marriage expenditure worth Rs.15,02,000/- and return of dowry of Rs.
10,00,000/- and also granted the return of gold chain and gold ring worth Rs.42,500/- since both the parties are not aggrieved by the decree of divorce granted by the Family Court in the said O.P. ii.

The appellant herein shall take all steps through his father Sri Upender Maheswaram, Defacto complainant in C.C. No.
2200/2018 at Il Addl.

Judicial First Class Magistrate at Hanamkonda, to tender Abhishek Maheshwaram vs Ms. Sindu Pendota on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196901819/
1 no-objection or not to oppose the quash petition vide CRLP No. 13420 of 2024 in lieu of the compromise arrived between the parties or to get a compromise recorded in the said case before the Trial Court for withdrawal or closure of the same.
iii. The respondent who is a de-facto complainant in C.C. No. 638 of 2017 on the file of XIII Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad for the offences of S.498A,
406, 420, 506 and 354 of IPC, and S. 4 & 6 of DP Act; and as the said criminal proceedings are only continued against the appellant herein as the said proceedings against the other accused's since were quashed in quash petitions filed by the other accused's, by virtue of this compromise and as a part of the settlement undertakes to withdraw or compromise in the said proceedings either before the Trial Court or before Lok-Adalat and or to tender no- objection in the event of any quash petition that may be filed before this Hon'ble Court by the appellant for closure of the said criminal proceedings.

sentences.text: iv. The parties hereto have entered into this compromise with their free will and consent and declare that, with the compromise recorded in this memorandum there are no pending disputes, issues, things recoverable by them form either of the parties and further undertake that, either themselves or through their family members or through any acquaintances shall not interfere in future with their individual personal marital lives and shall not indulge in any acts of purporting to cause disturbance and having the effect of maligning reputation of their respective families in the society"

4. In terms of the specific terms of settlement arrived at between the parties, they have also moved an interlocutory i.e., I.A.No.1 of 2024 dated 10.12.2024 for the disposal of the present appeal in terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that in terms of the settlement recorded and envisaged in the preceding paragraphs, the appellant as of now intends not to pursue the appeal any further.

However, he only expresses that let the respondent also take necessary steps in abiding by the conditions stipulated in the terms of settlement so far as the closure of the criminal cases before the different criminal courts, which has been accepted by the learned counsel, as has already been reflected in the terms and conditions.
6. In view of the said terms of settlement, I.A.No.1 of 2024 and the appeal as of now stands disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
